questions.stem: The BHAKRA DAM — India's second-tallest dam — is built on which river?
questions.explanation: BHAKRA DAM — concrete gravity dam on SUTLEJ RIVER at BHAKRA village (Bilaspur district, Himachal Pradesh, near Punjab border). Height: 226 metres (India's 2nd-tallest dam after Tehri; earlier the TALLEST when built). Length: 520 m. Construction: 1948-63; inaugurated by JAWAHARLAL NEHRU who called India's dams 'TEMPLES OF MODERN INDIA'. Creates GOBIND SAGAR reservoir (named after 10th Sikh Guru Gobind Singh) — 168 km² surface, 90km long. BHAKRA-NANGAL is the PAIR: Nangal Dam is 13km downstream (a barrage for irrigation + flood regulation). Power: 1325 MW total generation. Irrigates 10 million acres in Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan. Managed by BBMB (Bhakra Beas Management Board). Bhakra Main Canal feeds Indira Gandhi Canal system in Rajasthan. Called 'NEW TEMPLE OF INDIA' by Nehru (1963 speech). DAM vs BARRAGE distinction: Dam is tall, stores water; barrage is low-height with gates, diverts/regulates.

questions.stem: Match dam to river: (A) Sardar Sarovar (B) Hirakud (C) Nagarjuna Sagar (D) Mettur
questions.explanation: MAJOR DAM-RIVER MAPPINGS (memorise): SARDAR SAROVAR — NARMADA (Gujarat; world's 2nd-largest concrete gravity dam by volume; controversial — anti-NBA movement by Medha Patkar). HIRAKUD — MAHANADI (Odisha; WORLD'S LONGEST EARTHEN DAM at 25.8 km main + dykes; India's FIRST major multi-purpose river valley project post-independence, 1956). NAGARJUNA SAGAR — KRISHNA (AP-Telangana border; world's largest masonry dam). METTUR (STANLEY RESERVOIR) — CAUVERY (Tamil Nadu). TEHRI — BHAGIRATHI (Uttarakhand; India's tallest at 260m). BHAKRA — SUTLEJ (HP/Punjab). KOYNA — KOYNA (Maharashtra). IDUKKI — PERIYAR (Kerala; double-curvature arch — India's only such dam, 3rd in Asia). KRISHNA RAJA SAGAR (KRS) — CAUVERY (Karnataka). TUNGABHADRA — TUNGABHADRA (KA-AP). GANDHI SAGAR — CHAMBAL (MP-Raj). FARAKKA (barrage) — GANGA (WB). RIHAND — SON (UP). SRISAILAM — KRISHNA (AP). UKAI — TAPI (Gujarat). BAN SAGAR — SON. INDIRASAGAR — NARMADA (MP).

questions.stem: The SARDAR SAROVAR DAM on the Narmada River was inaugurated by PM Modi in 2017. The project also involves the construction of the world's TALLEST statue — which is:

options.option_text: STATUE OF UNITY of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel (182 m tall)
Statue of Lord Ram in Ayodhya
Statue of Buddha at Bodh Gaya

questions.explanation: STATUE OF UNITY — statue of SARDAR VALLABHBHAI PATEL (1875-1950, India's first Home Minister + Deputy PM; 'IRON MAN OF INDIA' — integrated 562 princely states into the Indian Union by 1949). Located at SADHU BET island, 3.5 km downstream of SARDAR SAROVAR DAM on the NARMADA RIVER, Kevadia (now renamed Ektanagar), Narmada district, GUJARAT. HEIGHT: 182 metres (597 ft) — TALLEST statue in the world. Unveiled 31 OCTOBER 2018 by PM Modi on Patel's 143rd birth anniversary (observed as RASHTRIYA EKTA DIVAS — National Unity Day). Statue designed by India's Ram V. Sutar; constructed by L&T. Cost: ~₹3000 Cr. Previously tallest: Spring Temple Buddha (China, 128 m). Under construction: Shivaji statue in Arabian Sea (Mumbai), Ram Statue at Ayodhya, planned to surpass — all in coming years. Surrounding Kevadia area now developed as a tourism hub ('Tent City', Valley of Flowers, zoo, etc.).

questions.stem: Nehru called dams the 'TEMPLES OF MODERN INDIA'. The FIRST major post-Independence multi-purpose river-valley project was:

options.option_text: DAMODAR VALLEY CORPORATION (DVC) — modeled on Tennessee Valley Authority, established 1948

questions.explanation: DVC (Damodar Valley Corporation) — established 7 July 1948, India's FIRST multi-purpose river valley authority. Modeled after the USA's TENNESSEE VALLEY AUTHORITY (TVA, 1933, New Deal). Objective: harness the DAMODAR RIVER (formerly 'Sorrow of Bengal' — caused frequent floods) for flood control, irrigation, hydroelectric power, coal-based thermal power, soil conservation. DAMS built under DVC: TILAIYA (Barakar river, 1953), KONAR (Konar river, 1955), MAITHON (Barakar, 1957), PANCHET (Damodar, 1959). Together with barrages at Durgapur + Bermo. Damodar used to cause huge annual floods in Bengal; DVC largely tamed it. Covers parts of Jharkhand + West Bengal. Significance: MAJOR pioneer in India's planned development + river valley development. Today, DVC also runs thermal + power trading. BHAKRA NANGAL came later (1963) — Nehru's famous 'Temples of Modern India' quote about Bhakra. RIHAND on Son river (Sonebhadra, UP) — built 1954-62. INDIRASAGAR, SARDAR SAROVAR etc. are all later.

questions.stem: The INDIRA GANDHI CANAL (IGC) — the LONGEST canal in India — flows through which state, bringing water from the Sutlej-Beas river system to arid areas?

options.option_text: RAJASTHAN (transforms Thar desert fringe — Ganga Nagar, Hanumangarh, Bikaner, Jaisalmer)

questions.explanation: INDIRA GANDHI CANAL (IGC) — formerly RAJASTHAN CANAL; renamed 1984 in honour of Indira Gandhi. LONGEST canal in India: ~650 km (plus ~1,750 km of branches). Originates from HARIKE BARRAGE (at Sutlej-Beas confluence, Punjab — 40 km long Rajasthan Feeder Canal goes through Ferozepur + into Ganganagar district Rajasthan). Flows through: Ganganagar, Hanumangarh, Churu, Bikaner, Jaisalmer, Jodhpur, Barmer (NW Rajasthan — the Thar desert edge). Transformed arid desert lands into agricultural regions — wheat, cotton, mustard, gram now grown. CONCEIVED by Kanwar Sain (1948, engineer). Construction STARTED 1958 (1st phase inaugurated 1961 by Nehru). Phase 2 (to Jaisalmer) completed 1986. Criticism: waterlogging + salinity in some areas; ecological + sociological disruption; not reached easternmost target areas. Still India's greatest irrigation project by length/coverage. OTHER MAJOR CANALS: UPPER GANGA CANAL (world's largest irrigation canal system when built 1854 by Proby Cautley); SUTLEJ-YAMUNA LINK (SYL) — partially built, litigated Punjab-Haryana; NARMADA MAIN CANAL from Sardar Sarovar (458 km).

questions.stem: The NARMADA BACHAO ANDOLAN (NBA) — a grassroots social movement opposing big dams — particularly targeted the Sardar Sarovar Project. Who was its primary leader?

options.option_text: MEDHA PATKAR (along with Baba Amte, Arundhati Roy support)

questions.explanation: NARMADA BACHAO ANDOLAN (NBA, 'Save the Narmada Movement') — a social movement launched 1989, primarily led by MEDHA PATKAR (Magsaysay Award 1992, Right Livelihood Award 1991). BABA AMTE (revered social activist, leprosy work) also supported. NOVELIST ARUNDHATI ROY wrote influential essays supporting it. Objections: (1) displacement of ~300,000 tribal + local people; (2) inadequate rehabilitation; (3) submergence of forests + fertile lands; (4) benefits more to rich farmers in far-off Gujarat than to affected peoples in MP/Maharashtra. SC case Narmada Bachao Andolan v. Union (2000): SC allowed continued construction with conditions on rehabilitation. Height was raised in phases. SARDAR SAROVAR finally inaugurated at full height in 2017 by PM Modi. OTHER ECO-MOVEMENTS: CHIPKO MOVEMENT (1970s, Uttarakhand, led by Sunderlal Bahuguna + Chandi Prasad Bhatt + Gaura Devi — hugged trees to save forests); SILENT VALLEY MOVEMENT (1970s-80s, Kerala, KSSP against hydroelectric project in Silent Valley rainforest — SUCCESS, dam cancelled, area became national park); APPIKO (1983, Karnataka, inspired by Chipko); JUNGLE BACHAO (Jharkhand); TEHRI DAM PROTESTS.

questions.stem: The MULLAPERIYAR DAM — a century-old dam — has been a source of dispute between which two Indian states?

options.option_text: Kerala (where the dam is located) and Tamil Nadu (which leases + operates it)

questions.explanation: MULLAPERIYAR DAM — on PERIYAR RIVER in IDUKKI DISTRICT, KERALA. Built 1895 by the British (John Pennycuick, engineer) — 120+ years old. LEASED to Madras Presidency for 999 years under a 1886 treaty between Travancore + British. Since Independence, TAMIL NADU (successor to Madras) continues to OPERATE the dam and DIVERT Periyar waters through a tunnel under the Western Ghats to the Vaigai basin (for irrigation in Theni, Madurai). KERALA owns the land + surrounding area; wants the old dam decommissioned + replaced due to safety concerns (earthquake-prone zone, old lime-surki masonry). TAMIL NADU wants the dam preserved + water level raised (for its farmers). SC multiple rulings generally favouring TN's operational rights. Other inter-state water disputes: CAUVERY (Karnataka-TN-Puducherry-Kerala), KRISHNA (Maharashtra-Karnataka-AP-Telangana), GODAVARI (inter-state tribunal); RAVI-BEAS-SUTLEJ (Punjab-Haryana-Rajasthan — Sutlej Yamuna Link canal dispute). Under Art 262 + Inter-State River Water Disputes Act 1956, tribunals resolve such disputes — though often appealed in SC.
